chapter: Louis Armstrong, King Oliver and St. Louis memories
title: Meeting King Oliver in Savannah
summary: While on tour with Claude Hopkins, Thomas met King Oliver at Tybee Beach near Savannah, and later told Pops about it.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: He was by himself. They were doing things like they'd thank come out of town, than you, Baby, they'd come out of town. They'd come from Chicago. They might have been working with -- I don't know. No, I think it was Carol Dickerson's band but they might have been working with Joe Oliver during that time but I thought Joe Oliver was a great trumpet player. Had a chance to meet him in Savannah, Georgia. some years ago.
You did? Who were you down there with?
Claude Hopkins.
King Oliver was still alive then?
Yeah.
And you did meet him?
Joe King Oliver is one of my great pleasures. I told
JT (1 of 2)
Pops about him.
What did you have to say to him?
It was a funny damn thing about that.
What shape was he in?
(Singly he was in very good shape.
What was he doing? Was that when he was running the fruit stand?
He came out to the place where we were staying so I asked the guy. Tydeo Beach was the place where you get off the nut. The bandleader gets off the nut
What's the name of the place?
Tydeo Beach. T-y-b-e-e.
That's near Atlanta, is it?
Savannah, Georgia. And I just left a good friend of ours, terrific pianist, by the name of Connie Berry, a good friend of Babe's. They worked together.
Never heard of her.
No, Connie, she's a little girl. Beautiful
Where is she? Is she planning on playing jazz piano?
Anything. And, so this particular time we went to Atlanta (end of side 1, tape 2)
